worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(0):$

$$
v(0)=⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\times a(0),||v(0)||,$ and $||v(0)\times a(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\times a(0) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}, \\ ||v(0)\times a(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(0)\times a(0)||}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $1\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$
